title: Multimodal Cross-Device and Marker-Free Co-Registration of Preclinical Imaging Modalities
protocol: Load volumes into analysis software as two different layers called "underlay" and "overlay".
Use the underlay rendering to inspect an anatomically detailed dataset.
Utilize the overlay, rendered transparently, to visualize additional information within the image.
Display the signal distribution of a tracer-based modality in the overlay layer.
Switch between underlay and overlay layers by pressing tab.
Select the desired layer directly from the dropdown list in the top toolbar.
Affect editing operations on the currently selected layer.
Prepare a suitable multimodal carrier for the phantom.
Fix the phantom on the carrier using material that does not impair image quality.
Place the carrier in the imaging device reliably and reproducibly.
Acquire a scan with a large field of view covering the entire phantom.
This first image is referred to as "Image A".
Include all fiducials in Image A for calculating differential transformation matrix.
Remove the carrier from the imaging device.
Replace the carrier in the imaging device.
Perform a second scan using a significantly smaller field of view.
Load image A as underlay in the analysis software.
Choose the image file for underlay and click on open.
Press [Alt + 3] to activate the 3D view if it is not present.
Adjust the windowing by pressing [Ctrl + W].
Move the left and right vertical bars to clearly distinguish the phantom or tracers.
Click on Okay to close the dialog.
Load image B as overlay in the analysis software.
Choose the image file for overlay and click on open.
Check Iso rendering under Menu 3D-Rendering > Overlay mode.
Visually check if the imaging device and the method of placing the phantom are self-consistent.
Ensure that the phantom is fully aligned in underlay and overlay.
Check that the yellow rendering is a subset of the white rendering.
Open the analysis software.
Load the CT image as underlay using Menu File > Underlay > Load underlay.
Choose the image file for underlay and press open.
Load the PET image as overlay using Menu File > Overlay > Load Overlay.
Choose the image file for overlay and press open.
Show axial slice view by pressing [Alt + A].
Show sagittal slice view by pressing [Alt + S].
Show coronal slice view by pressing [Alt + C].
Perform marker-based fusion.
Switch the view to only show the underlay: Menu View > Layer Settings > Layer Visibility > uncheck overlay; Menu View > Layer Settings > Layer Visibility > check underlay.
Switch the selected layer to the underlay.
If necessary, adjust the windowing: Press [Ctrl + W] and adjust the left and right vertical bars in the following dialog to better see the fiducials. Click on Okay to close the dialog.
Activate the mouse action mode "create marker" by clicking the marker symbol on the vertical toolbar on the left side.
Navigate to a fiducial. To this end, place the mouse pointer over the view of a plane and use [Alt + mouse wheel] to slice through the planes.
Place the mouse pointer on the center of the fiducial and left-click.
Keep the suggested name, e.g., "Marker001," and click on ok to save the marker.
Adjust the viewing settings to show the overlay: Menu View > Layer Settings > Layer Visibility > check overlay.
Align the markers of underlay and overlay.
Compute rotation and translation (markers).
Note the residual of fusion measurement.
Click on ok to confirm alignment.
Check that markers in the underlay and overlay visually match.
Press [Ctrl + I] to display details of new overlay transformation.
Activate views of both layers: check underlay and overlay.
Activate mouse mode "interactive image fusion".
Ensure settings toolbar for the mouse mode appears.
Check overlay checkbox, uncheck underlay and segmentation checkboxes.
Interactively align the overlay to the underlay by performing rotations and translations.
Place the mouse pointer near the edge of a view (axial, coronal or sagittal).
Hold the left mouse button and move the mouse to rotate the overlay.
Place the mouse pointer near the center of a view.
Hold the left mouse button and move the mouse to move the overlay.
Menu Fusion > Overlay transformation > Create and save differential transformation.
Select the original overlay file and click on Open.
Enter a file name for the differential transformation and press Save.
Fix the sample (e.g., a sedated laboratory animal) on the carrier.
Place the carrier in the CT device.
Ensure to place the carrier in the same way as was done during the calibration scan.
Scan according to the instructions of the device's manufacturer.
Place the carrier in the PET device.
Ensure to place the carrier in the same way as was done during the calibration scan.
Scan according to the device's manufacturer instructions.
Perform application of the differential transformation.
Open the analysis software.
Load CT file as underlay: Menu File > Underlay > Load underlay. In the dialog, choose the CT image file and press ok.
Load PET file as overlay: Menu File > Overlay > Load overlay. In the dialog, choose the PET image file and press ok.
Activate the views of both layers: Menu View > Layer Settings > Layer Visibility > check underlay; Menu View > Layer Settings > Layer Visibility > check overlay.

Load and apply the previously saved differential transformation matrix: Menu > Fusion > Overlay transformation > Load and apply transform. Select the file containing the differential transformation matrix from the calibration process and press open.
Save the altered overlay: Menu > File > Overlay > Save overlay. In the dialog, enter a new name and click on save.
